column1: # doc 61 -- first 20 events of the d59k scan set, scanned by Claude 2026-07-26,
# NOT yet validated by the owner.  Same verdicts are in nusel_labels/c59k/.
# Overlay onto the display with:  serve_nusel_scan.sh ... --ai-scan <this file>
# verdict: STM | nu      <- the scan's decision, two values only.  The set has
#   already had TGM- and LM-tagged events removed (doc 59), so a bundle that is
#   not a stopping muon stays a NEUTRINO CANDIDATE (owner, 2026-07-26).
# quality: clean | weak | cosmic-like | junk | unclear   <- why to trust it or
#   not; NOT a verdict.  cosmic-like = topology reads as a cosmic (through-going
#   or truncated with no Bragg) even though it is not STM; junk = the cluster is
#   not one physical object; unclear = a reconstruction pathology dominates.

column10: reason
single 130 cm track, enters upstream wall z~2 (outside FV), textbook Bragg to 165 ke/cm at rr=0 (ks1=0.010), charge spray at the stopping end = Michel candidate

NOT STM: the end the fit calls stopping has FLAT MIP dQ/dx to rr=0, no Bragg -> it is truncated, not stopped. Exits the bottom wall y=-198 and carries several 10-20 cm side prongs along its length, no single vertex -- reads cosmic, but it is not a stopping muon
the STM tag is wrong here: flat 50-55 ke/cm right down to rr=0, no Bragg; upper end just stops mid-detector, lower end exits the bottom wall. (Owner's own comment on this bundle: "Not STM")
NOT STM: enters the top wall y=200 at (172,63), kinks at (191,173,22), and BOTH arms reach the anode plane x=201 -> through-going, nothing stops. (tgm=0, so TGM missed it)
fully contained clean V: apex (132,56,180), two ~20 cm arms, dense high-charge blob at one end
94 pts in ~8 disconnected blobs over 150 cm (1.4 pts/cm); no track to judge
300 cm cathode crosser entering the upstream wall z~2, stops at (12,-190,234); textbook Bragg on the TPC1 side (ks1=0.018)

vertex (126,-106,497) just inside the downstream wall, 3.4 cm stub toward the wall + 47 cm prong with a Bragg end; the wall contact is GRAZING (track parallel to the wall), not an entry. (Owner called this one a nu candidate, on its kinks)
one 10 cm dense clump at (-137,-124,420) + ~10 stray dots over 90 cm + a fragment 200 cm away
a single 2.2 cm blob at (-105,-191,64) plus 2 unrelated fragments at the downstream wall
vertex (-19,-33,300): 10 cm stub at 3.24 MIP (dQ/dx spikes to 300 ke/cm at rr<2, well ABOVE the muon curve = proton-like) + 300 cm MIP prong exiting the downstream wall along +z (beam direction)
single smooth 96 cm contained track, both ends inside, no vertex activity; no dQ/dx available (STM skipped it as contained)
4 dots + fragments across the whole TPC; STM could not even build a steiner tree (stmfit=nosteiner)

157 cm contained cathode crosser, straight in X-Y but a clear slope break in z exactly at x=0 -> suspect a cathode-join / z artifact, not a physical kink. Pre-un-merge bundle also holds a top-wall blob at (8,195,73)
dozens of disconnected short fragments hugging the anode plane x~-200 over 150 cm in z; only a 16 cm piece is fittable
165 cm near-vertical track at essentially constant z (dz=7 cm over 165 cm = prolonged w.r.t. the collection wires) with a T-branch at y=-74; contained but reads like a partly-reconstructed cosmic
vertex (92,29,450): ~8 cm stub + 60 cm prong exiting the downstream wall; STM rejected on "extra tracks" -- correct. Event also has a 205 PE in-beam flash with no bundle
128 cm contained, 5 cm hook at the upper end (y -168->-163) and a 2-prong fork at the lower end (-16,-193,236); cannot be a cosmic muon (crosses no boundary)

253 cm contained cathode crosser, y from -103 to +76 = near-vertical and nearly perpendicular to the beam, Y fork at the top end; no gray charge continues past either end, but a 180 cm vertical contained track is cosmic-shaped
~8 dots in a 20 cm cloud + fragments 250 cm away (145 pts / 56 cm)
